elements.content: Grammar focus: All, Both, Either, Neither, None.

Count first: two things take both, either or neither; three or more take all or none. Then match the verb: both and all plural, either and neither singular, none singular in formal writing and plural in speech. Never write both of them was, and never use neither with three things.

both + plural verb — two, affirmative: both proposals were rejected
either + singular verb — one of two, any: either option works
neither + singular verb — two, negative: neither proposal was acceptable
all + plural verb — three or more, affirmative: all the bids were opened
none of + plural noun — three or more, negative: none of the bids was opened
not either / neither ... nor — negative of two: neither the chair nor the members replied
Guided practice: choose the correct option.
1. Complete: '___ of the two plans was approved.'
2. Complete: 'Both proposals ___ rejected.'
3. Which is correct for three or more?
options: None of the three bids was opened.
Neither of the three bids was opened.

elements.content: Read and listen: three examples in context.

Both reports were late. — Two, affirmative, plural verb. (Both + plural.)
Neither report was complete. — Two, negative, singular verb. (Neither + singular in formal use.)
None of the reports was complete. — More than two, negative. (None of + plural noun.)
What do you observe?

Both, either and neither work with two things. Both is affirmative and takes a plural verb. Either means one or the other, and takes a singular verb. Neither means not one and not the other, and is singular in careful use. All and none work with three or more: all takes a plural verb when it means every one, none can take either, with the singular preferred in formal writing.
1. Which quantifier refers to exactly two things?
2. Which verb follows 'both proposals'?
State the rule in one sentence, without looking at the table.
Freer production: I can summarise data using quantifiers.

Success criteria:
- I can use both, either and neither for two things.
- I can use all and none for three or more.
- I can match the verb to the quantifier.
Role play: put your position in ninety seconds; your partner notes every use of the target structure.
Frequent errors and correction:

❌ Both of the proposals was rejected (singular verb after both) → ✅ Both of the proposals were rejected
❌ None of the three report was complete (singular noun after none of) → ✅ None of the three reports was complete
Correct these sentences: say what is wrong, then give the right version.
Acceptable variants:

Neither of the two suppliers met the deadline.
None of the three suppliers met the deadline.
Either candidate would suit the role.
Adapt the same task to the group:

- Individual: five sentences with the structure, on the topic of the lesson.
- Pair: a ten-line dialogue where all, both, either, neither, none carries the argument.
- Group: a six-minute debate, two sides, the structure required in every turn.
- Professional audience: transpose the structure into a memo.
- Academic audience: transpose it into a paragraph of analysis.
